khemā.notes: AN 8.91–117 names Khemā in the list of laywomen. DPPN suggests she may have become the nun, but the text supplies no link. AN 6.49 names the monk Khema, and kheme migadāye in DN 14 is Vipassī’s deer park at Bandhumatī. Thig 6.3 also addresses the nun as kheme at 1.4, one segment after her name in English. The relevant passages in the cited page ranges are AN 1.236, AN 2.131 and SN 17.24 for the nun, and AN 8.91–117 for the laywoman.

khiḍḍāpadosikā.notes: The packet reports zero mentions. DN 1 at 2.7.2 and DN 24 at 2.18.9 explicitly say khiḍḍāpadosikā nāma devā, and DN 20 at 16.3 lists them at the assembly. Sujato translates the name as ‘depraved by play’, so the English name filter misses the group.

khomadussa.notes: SN 7.22 opens in the Sakyan town of Khomadussa. The page also includes SN 8.1, where Vaṅgīsa is staying at Āḷavī.

khujjuttarā.notes: AN 1.260 singles her out for learning. AN 2.133 and SN 17.24 pair her with Nandamātā as a model laywoman. The neighboring AN groups and SN 17.23 and 17.25 in the citation list omit her. DPD’s SN 17.16 hint also misses her in the app’s numbering.

kikī.notes: DN 14 names Kikī as king at Varanasi in Kassapa’s lifetime, and MN 81 calls him king of Kāsi. The entries disagree about his daughter Dhammā’s later birth. This entry names Dhammadinnā, while the Kisā Gotamī entry names Kisā Gotamī.

kimikālā.notes: AN 9.3 and Ud 4.1 both place Meghiya’s mango grove on the Kimikāḷā after his almsround in Jantugāma. AN 9.2 is an adjacent discourse.

kinnughaṇḍu.notes: DN 20 at 10.6 spells the name kinnighaṇḍu, which has its own DPD lemma. DN 32 at 10.5 spells it kinnughaṇḍu. Both lists pair him with Nighaṇḍu, and Sujato uses Kinnughaṇḍu in both. The DN 20 spelling lacks the DPPN match in the candidate data.

kisāgotamī.notes: AN 1.246 names the nun foremost in wearing coarse robes, and SN 5.3 recounts her encounter with Māra. The packet misses Thig 10.1, where the verse at 11.3 and the attribution at 12.1 spell her name in two words, Kisā gotamī. The neighboring AN 1.219–234 and 1.248–257 groups lack her name.

kokanada.notes: MN 85 at 2.1 explicitly names Prince Bodhi’s newly built mansion. Its name also occurs at 5.1 and 8.2 in forms shared with other senses. The SN 1.39 and 1.40 matches refer to Pajjunna’s daughters and belong under kokanadā.

kokanadā.notes: The single entry covers both daughters. SN 1.39 names Kokanadā, and SN 1.40 introduces Cūḷakokanadā and calls her Kokanadā in the verse. The reference lands on SN 1.38 as well, but that discourse concerns the Buddha’s splinter injury.

kokanuda.notes: AN 10.96 names the wanderer who questions Ānanda at the hot springs. Sujato spells his name Kokanada. The hit at AN 10.100 is the chapter’s closing summary verse referring back to AN 10.96.

kokālika.notes: AN 10.89, SN 6.10 and Snp 3.10 recount his accusation against Sāriputta and Moggallāna. SN 6.9 has Tudu’s visit to the sick monk. The SN 6.8 citation lands on a verse about Katamorakatissaka. Snp 1.7 is another false hit from the entry’s Snp page reference.

komudī.notes: This sense names a calendar day. DN 2 and MN 118 both explicitly identify the Komudī full moon of the fourth month.

korabya.notes: The packet reports zero mentions because Sujato spells the name Koravya. MN 82 at 27.1 names rājā korabyo, the king who questions Raṭṭhapāla. AN 6.54 at 9.1 names a king of the past, owner of the banyan Suppatiṭṭha. DPPN describes both under this royal name. Thag 16.4 preserves Raṭṭhapāla’s verses addressing a king without giving his name.
